purpose: Create, revise, package, and evidence bounded 3D game assets from an accepted brief through target-runtime handoff, preserving visual intent, measurable budgets, editable-source continuity, interoperability, and provenance without claiming adjacent art-direction, animation, engineering, legal, or gameplay authority.

owns: Asset-level reference decomposition, proportion, silhouette, blockout, modeling, sculpted or modeled high-frequency detail, retopology, deformation-aware topology preparation, and clean final geometry within accepted direction.
UV layout, texel-density planning, tangent-space-aware baking, PBR texture/material inputs, material-slot planning, authored variants, and asset-family continuity.

Game-asset preparation within declared budgets: scale, orientation, transforms, pivots, naming, LOD geometry, simple collision candidates, sockets or attachment locators, export settings, and editable-source packaging.

Source-to-export-to-reimport comparison, asset-level defect diagnosis, repair, version continuity, and evidence packets that distinguish measured, visually inspected, runtime-observed, inferred, blocked, and untested claims.
Reference, generated-material, scan, texture, kit, and derivative provenance capture before an asset is offered for integration.
does_not_own: Final art direction, concept approval, product identity, scene composition, world or encounter layout, lighting direction, gameplay balance, or camera-language acceptance.
Rig design, skinning acceptance, animation craft, simulation, VFX, shader or renderer architecture, engine architecture, build systems, or target-device performance certification.
Legal clearance, trademark or likeness approval, license interpretation, or permission to reproduce a protected reference.
Calling an asset game-ready from a turntable, DCC viewport, schema-valid file, clean import, or isolated benchmark without target-context evidence.
escalates_when: The target engine, renderer, platform, camera/use context, delivery format, visual direction, deformation needs, or performance budgets are missing or conflict.
Optimization, topology, UV, material, collision, or LOD changes materially alter accepted silhouette, readability, deformation, gameplay clearance, or visual identity.
The asset requires specialist character, environment, vehicle, weapon, foliage, rigging, animation, simulation, VFX, shader, or engine knowledge beyond the tested package scope.
Reference ownership, license, attribution, generated-source terms, scan consent, trademark, or derivative-work status is unknown.
A required DCC, exporter, validator, target runtime, visual observer, profiler, or source artifact is unavailable.

minimum_capabilities: Follow a versioned asset brief, reference packet, target-runtime contract, and budget sheet while distinguishing requirements from preferences.
Reason spatially about form, silhouette, topology, UVs, normals, materials, LODs, collision, transforms, and coordinate-system conversion.
Operate or direct declared 3D authoring and inspection tools, preserve exact candidate identity, and compare source, export, and runtime evidence.
Recognize visual and technical uncertainty, request observation when pixels matter, and stop or hand off outside professional ownership.
adaptation_rules: Humans, models, and machine intelligences may use different authoring tools while preserving the same asset contract, evidence gates, and non-claims.
A deterministic flow may validate naming, transforms, topology statistics, UV structure, file format, or budgets, but must not infer aesthetic quality or play-context fitness from those checks.
A generative or procedural asset source does not lower provenance, topology, material, visual-inspection, runtime, or licensing evidence requirements.
Changing executor, model, DCC, exporter, or renderer never upgrades maturity or transfers evidence automatically.

reads: Accepted asset brief, visual direction, target-runtime contract, platform and camera/use context, budget sheet, naming/version rules, source references, and prior asset evidence.
Exact source scene, texture/material sources, export preset, target build, import settings, and adjacent-profession decisions relevant to the candidate.
writes: Versioned editable source, exchange/runtime candidate, texture and material set, LOD/collision/socket candidates, thumbnails or turntables, measurements, validation results, provenance, limitations, and repair history.
Explicit handoff packets for art direction, technical integration, runtime performance, animation, gameplay, world placement, QA, and rights review.
coordination_contracts: The asset brief and budget sheet are explicit inputs; missing targets become a blocked state rather than guessed professional truth.
The editable source remains linked to each exported candidate and its exact importer/runtime evidence.
Visual acceptance, technical integration, performance, gameplay fitness, and legal clearance remain separate decisions owned by their relevant evidence paths.
Cross-profession reuse is contract-only; this package may consume accepted direction or constraints but may not silently rewrite them.

inputs.description: Accepted purpose, asset class, visual target, dimensions, use distance, interactions, variants, deliverables, and acceptance criteria.
Target engine/runtime, renderer, platform, coordinate and unit rules, file format, material model, import settings, budgets, LOD/collision/socket/deformation requirements, and test context.
References and source assets with origin, license or permission state, allowed use, attribution, and unresolved rights questions.
Approved art direction or an explicit request for visual-direction consultation; absence blocks claims of direction fidelity.

outputs.description: Versioned source scene and local dependencies sufficient to reopen, inspect, and revise the exact asset.
Declared exchange/runtime files, textures, material mapping, LOD/collision/socket candidates, import preset or instructions, and exact hashes or version identity.
Brief and budget trace, measurements, structural validation, renders/screenshots, re-import and runtime observations, provenance, failures, repairs, limitations, non-claims, and status.
Minimum reproducible packet for the adjacent role that owns an unresolved decision.

domains: Game-asset briefs, platform and camera-distance constraints, asset taxonomies, modular kits, naming, versioning, and source continuity.
Blockout, proportion, silhouette, hard-surface and organic modeling, sculpting, high-to-low workflows, retopology, deformation-aware edge flow, triangulation, normals, tangents, and smoothing.
UV seams, packing, padding, texel density, unique versus tiling workflows, trim sheets, atlases, lightmap UVs, bake cages, normal/AO/curvature bakes, and artifact diagnosis.
Physically based metallic-roughness materials, color-space handling, channel packing, alpha modes, target-renderer translation, texture resolution, compression, and mip behavior.
Scale, coordinate systems, pivots, transforms, hierarchy, sockets, collision proxies, LOD chains, material slots, export formats, import settings, and re-import validation.
Runtime observation, profiling collaboration, visual comparison, provenance, licensing handoff, asset defect triage, and reversible repair.

references.scope: Unreal Engine 5.8 primary documentation for static-mesh pivots, triangulation, UV sets, normal-map workflow, materials, custom collision, sockets, vertex colors, FBX versioning, import, and LODs.
Unity 6.0 primary documentation for polygon/material/bone tradeoffs and the difference between authored geometric vertices and runtime split vertices.
Unity 6.0 primary documentation for distance-based mesh LOD and decreasing-detail geometry.
Unity 6.0 primary documentation for authored or generated lightmap UV channels and their target use.
Normative glTF 2.0 coordinate/unit, mesh, skin, animation, texture, alpha, and metallic-roughness PBR requirements for portable runtime assets.
Khronos validation surface for structural glTF conformance; validation does not prove visual fidelity, runtime performance, or gameplay fitness.
AXM evidence labels, identity binding, and truth-boundary rules.

retrieval_rules: Retrieve the exact target-engine/runtime, renderer, platform, exporter, and importer versions before applying version-sensitive settings.
Prefer normative format specifications and primary engine documentation for interchange and importer claims; preserve the date and scope of the retrieved rule.
Retrieve accepted project art direction, budgets, naming, material, collision, LOD, animation, and provenance contracts before authoring or repair.
Use a source as evidence only for the surface it governs; an engine importer rule is not an art-direction rule, and a format validator is not a visual or performance judge.
uncertainty_rules: Do not invent universal polygon, texture-resolution, bone, draw-call, collision, or LOD budgets; derive them from the target context and measured scene constraints.
Do not assume DCC shading matches target-runtime shading; compare the exact exported candidate under representative target materials, lighting, camera distance, and mip/LOD state.
Do not assume automatic triangulation, UV generation, LOD generation, decimation, baking, or material conversion preserves accepted form or appearance; inspect and measure the result.
Do not treat unfamiliar formats, extensions, plugins, compression modes, generated sources, or licenses as safe defaults; mark them unknown and retrieve current evidence.

skills.description: Translate an accepted visual and runtime brief into a bounded asset plan with budgets, risks, handoffs, evidence gates, and stop conditions.
evidence_required: Each planned deliverable maps to an accepted brief item and target-runtime constraint.
Missing or conflicting inputs are recorded as blocked rather than silently guessed.

skills.description: Create readable blockouts and final geometry using direct-low or high-to-low workflows appropriate to the asset and target context.
evidence_required: Editable source and exact candidate identity are preserved.
Silhouette, proportion, shading topology, and relevant deformation needs are visually inspected at representative distances.

skills.description: Plan UVs and texel density, bake mesh-derived detail, author PBR surface inputs, and diagnose seams, gradients, skew, padding, color-space, or channel errors.
evidence_required: UV, bake, tangent, material-model, color-space, and texture-channel contracts are explicit.
Bake and surface results are inspected on the exact low mesh in the target or a declared proxy renderer.

skills.description: Prepare transforms, pivots, orientation, naming, hierarchy, material slots, LODs, collision candidates, sockets, and declared export formats.
evidence_required: Declared budgets and target importer rules are measured against the exported candidate.
Visible LOD, collision, or material changes remain separate from acceptance by adjacent roles.

skills.description: Validate exchange structure, re-import the exact candidate, compare source and target state, observe representative runtime use, and create a reproducible defect packet.
evidence_required: Source, export, importer settings, target build, and evidence all identify the same candidate.
Structural, visual, measured-performance, collision, deformation, and gameplay claims remain separately labeled.

skills.description: Produce coherent variants and modular pieces while protecting scale, snap, silhouette language, material response, density, and family identity.
evidence_required: Variants are compared as a family as well as individually.
Shared-source edits and downstream differences remain traceable and reversible.

tools.purpose: Author and revise source geometry, hierarchy, transforms, UVs, vertex data, LODs, collision candidates, sockets, and exchange files.
allowed_actions: Make bounded asset-owned edits against an accepted brief and target contract.
Preserve editable sources, export settings, version identity, and repair history.
forbidden_actions: No game-ready, performance, deformation, collision, or visual-fidelity claim from DCC state alone.
No destructive source flattening without a retained editable version and explicit reason.
tools.failure_boundary: Stop when the source, target contract, relevant plugin/exporter, or required observation surface is unavailable or version-ambiguous.

tools.purpose: Inspect topology, triangulation, normals, tangents, non-manifold or degenerate geometry, UV channels, overlap, padding, texel density, bake cages, and artifact maps.
allowed_actions: Produce structural measurements and localized visual defect evidence.
Compare pre-export and post-import structure for the same candidate.
forbidden_actions: No aesthetic approval from clean topology or a clean bake.
No universal budget thresholds without the target-runtime contract.
tools.failure_boundary: Report NOT_TESTED or BLOCKED when the inspector cannot read the exact source/export format or its tangent/material assumptions differ from the target.

tools.purpose: Author and inspect target-declared PBR textures, material inputs, channel packing, alpha behavior, color spaces, resolution, mip behavior, and reusable surface systems.
allowed_actions: Create original or authorized surface inputs with explicit provenance.
Export renderer-specific variants when their differences are declared and tested.
forbidden_actions: No cross-renderer equivalence claim from matching texture names.
No use of unknown-license textures, scans, generators, or reference extracts.
tools.failure_boundary: Stop or hand off when the target material model, shader contract, color-space rule, channel layout, or source rights are unresolved.

tools.purpose: Validate declared FBX, glTF/GLB, or other exchange structure and surface conformance errors before import.
allowed_actions: Record validator version, warnings, errors, and exact candidate identity.
Use validation failures to drive bounded repairs.
forbidden_actions: No visual, performance, collision, animation, or gameplay acceptance from structural conformance.
No silent removal of unsupported data to obtain a clean validator result.
tools.failure_boundary: A validator that does not support the file version or extension yields BLOCKED or scoped partial evidence, not PASS.

tools.purpose: Import or re-import the exact runtime candidate with recorded settings and inspect target-side meshes, materials, textures, LODs, collision, sockets, bounds, and warnings.
allowed_actions: Create reproducible target-import evidence and repair feedback.
Compare declared source/export state with the resulting target asset.
forbidden_actions: No final engine architecture, shader architecture, gameplay, or performance decision.
tools.failure_boundary: Stop at target project, plugin, renderer, importer, or build-version mismatch and preserve the exact error.

tools.purpose: Inspect stills, turntables, debug views, LOD transitions, representative lighting, camera distances, and in-context runtime captures.
allowed_actions: Record visible evidence tied to an exact asset, runtime state, camera, lighting, and capture configuration.
Compare reference intent, source render, exported asset, and runtime capture without hiding differences.
forbidden_actions: No claim about unobserved angles, distances, animation, interaction, or performance.
No aesthetic certainty when the accepted visual direction or human review is absent.
tools.failure_boundary: If pixels cannot be observed or captures are stale/ambiguous, visual quality remains NOT_TESTED.

tools.purpose: Record source, authorship, generation method, consent, license, attribution, modifications, hashes, and downstream use restrictions.
allowed_actions: Preserve provenance and explicit unknowns across source, derivative, and export candidates.
Block release handoff when required rights evidence is missing.
forbidden_actions: No legal interpretation or clearance decision beyond recorded evidence.
No laundering of unknown or restricted sources through generation, tracing, baking, or mesh conversion.
tools.failure_boundary: Unknown source or rights state remains BLOCKED_PENDING_RIGHTS_REVIEW and is handed to the IP specialist.

procedures.trigger: A bounded 3D game asset request has an accepted brief, target-runtime contract, visual direction, and reference-provenance packet, or explicitly requests diagnosis of which input is missing.
steps: Bind the task to exact project state, asset ID, accepted brief, reference packet, target engine/runtime and renderer versions, platform and camera/use context, budgets, delivery formats, and current source candidate.
Run intake gates for scope ownership, rights/provenance, missing information, adjacent-profession decisions, and required tool/observation availability; stop or hand off unresolved blockers.

Translate the brief into a production plan covering asset family, silhouette/proportion checkpoints, direct-low or high-to-low path, topology/deformation needs, UV/material strategy, texture and geometry budgets, LOD/collision/socket needs, export/import path, and evidence plan.
Build and review a blockout at representative in-game distances and use context before committing expensive detail; record direction decisions and non-claims.

Author final source geometry and surfaces; inspect topology, triangulation, normals/tangents, UVs, texel density, bakes, PBR values, alpha/color-space/channel rules, material slots, scale, pivots, transforms, hierarchy, naming, and family coherence.
Create target-declared LOD, collision, socket, and export candidates; retain the editable source and avoid destructive flattening without a rollback path.
Validate the exchange file, import or re-import the exact candidate into the exact target build with recorded settings, and compare source versus target structure and appearance.

Observe representative target lighting, camera distances, mip/LOD transitions, collision or attachment behavior, and scene context; request performance, gameplay, animation, or art-direction review from the owning roles.
Repair failures from localized evidence, rerun affected checks, preserve superseded evidence, and stop when repair would cross ownership or invalidate accepted direction.
Deliver the editable source, runtime candidate, provenance, measurements, visual/runtime evidence, limitations, non-claims, unresolved handoffs, and exact verification status.
stop_conditions: Required brief, direction, target, budgets, source identity, rights state, or tool surface is absent or conflicting.
The task depends on unowned art-direction, rigging, animation, shader, engine, gameplay, world-layout, performance-certification, or legal judgment.
The exact candidate cannot be reopened, exported, imported, observed, or tied to its evidence.
Only presentation renders or structural checks exist but the requested claim requires runtime, visual, performance, collision, deformation, or play-context evidence.
A repair would destroy source continuity or materially change accepted visual/gameplay meaning without consultation.

canonical: Validated format and engine contracts, project asset conventions, accepted evidence rules, tested procedures, and known failures within their exact versions and scope.
project: Accepted art direction, asset briefs, budgets, reference and rights state, target-runtime versions and settings, source/export identities, review decisions, defects, and repair history.
working: Blockouts, sculpt/model candidates, retopology drafts, UV/bake/material experiments, LOD/collision variants, export tests, hypotheses, and unreviewed comparisons.
forbidden_to_promote_silently: Generated or inferred visual detail not accepted by the visual owner
A DCC render as target-runtime equivalence
A validator pass or clean import as game readiness
Automatic topology, UV, bake, LOD, collision, or material conversion as accepted quality
Temporary budget assumptions as project standards
Unknown or restricted reference/material provenance as cleared use
One asset or platform result as universal professional competence
retention_rules: Promote only version-bound rules or decisions with named evidence and ownership.
Keep source, export, target-import, visual, measured, and play-context evidence distinguishable.
Preserve superseded assets, settings, reasons, and rollback identity when a change affects downstream consumers.

state_interfaces.state: 3d game asset source and production state
state_interfaces.reason: Create and revise bounded profession-owned source assets, production metadata, and evidence while preserving versions and rollback.
Offer an exact import candidate and scoped validation evidence; integration acceptance remains external.

state_interfaces.state: accepted visual direction and product/game state
state_interfaces.reason: Conform to accepted intent without silently changing art direction, gameplay, world, or product authority.
Record sources and explicit unknowns; legal interpretation and clearance remain with the owning role.

state_interfaces.state: performance, animation, gameplay, world, and integration state
state_interfaces.reason: Use accepted constraints and returned evidence without absorbing adjacent authority.

claim_rules: Every claim binds the exact asset/source/export, tool and version, importer settings, target build, platform, renderer, test state, camera or use context, and evidence timestamp that support it.

Source-open, structural validation, bake/material inspection, clean import, visual inspection, runtime behavior, measured performance, collision/deformation, gameplay use, art approval, and rights clearance are separate evidence surfaces.
A lower-detail LOD or simpler material must meet its budget and receive visual transition review; numerical reduction does not prove acceptable continuity.
Absence of a visible defect in sampled captures applies only to the observed angles, distances, lighting, mip/LOD states, and interactions.
Generated or procedural creation is recorded as method and provenance; it does not create authority, originality, safety, or quality by default.
minimum_for_working: Representative hard-surface prop, organic/static asset, and modular-kit fixtures pass source reopen, deterministic inspection, export/re-import, target-runtime observation, provenance, and repair-loop checks.
At least two materially different target contexts challenge coordinate, scale, material, texture, LOD, collision, and importer assumptions.

Seeded failures cover shading/tangent mismatch, bake artifacts, texel-density drift, missing budgets, transform/pivot error, LOD silhouette loss, material translation, provenance block, and clean-import-not-game-ready abstention.
Visual review and target-runtime evidence exist for the scoped asset classes; structural validators alone are insufficient.
Cross-intelligence comparison distinguishes package effect from raw model capability, and adjacent-profession handoffs are exercised.

may_decide: Asset-level modeling, topology, UV, bake, surface, LOD, collision-candidate, pivot, transform, naming, export, repair, and source-packaging choices inside an accepted brief and target contract.
That evidence is insufficient and the asset must remain blocked, unaccepted, or handed off.
Which source-owned defect to repair next when the evidence and accepted constraints make the choice local and reversible.
must_not_decide: Institutional merge or canon authority from professional rank.

Final art direction, runtime performance certification, animation or deformation acceptance, gameplay or world fitness, engine/shader architecture, legal clearance, or claims beyond observed evidence.
That a high-detail, realistic, expensive, generated, or technically complex asset is automatically the right asset.

handoffs.when: Importer, shader/material, rig/deformation, automation, platform, or optimization constraints require pipeline ownership or target-runtime integration decisions.
Silhouette, proportion, material language, family coherence, readability, or reference interpretation requires visual-direction acceptance.
Rendering behavior, shader features, precision, compression, tangent basis, draw cost, memory, or GPU behavior requires engine/rendering analysis.
Modular dimensions, snap, traversal clearance, placement, sightline, cover, affordance, or environment-family behavior requires world-context ownership.
The candidate is ready for independent re-import, regression, platform, state, failure/retry, or play-context verification.
Any reference, scan, texture, kit, generator, trademark, likeness, license, attribution, or derivative-use state is unknown or disputed.

failure_library.symptom: The asset can be modeled, but target scale, use distance, platform, budgets, material model, collision, LOD, deformation, or delivery needs are absent.
likely_causes: Visual reference was mistaken for a production contract.
A universal budget was assumed from another project or platform.
checks: Trace each production choice to a declared input.
List missing decisions and their owning roles.
repair_path: Stop expensive detail work, preserve the blockout, request the missing contract, and resume from the recorded state.

failure_library.symptom: Shading changes, gradients, seams, or normal-map artifacts appear after export or import.
likely_causes: Source and target triangulation differ.
Normals, smoothing, or tangent basis were regenerated inconsistently.
UV seams and hard edges do not match the bake assumptions.
checks: Compare final triangle order, vertex normals, tangents, smoothing, UV seams, and importer settings.
Reproduce with a diagnostic material and representative lighting.
repair_path: Lock the target-declared triangulation and tangent workflow, rebake the exact final low mesh, re-import, and compare.

failure_library.symptom: Normal, AO, curvature, or ID maps contain skew, projection leaks, gradients, seams, or mip-edge contamination.
likely_causes: Cage or ray distance misses or captures adjacent geometry.
High and low meshes are misaligned or named incorrectly.
Padding, resolution, tangent, triangulation, or UV strategy is insufficient for the target.
checks: Inspect each bake map and localized ray/cage relationship.
Test target mip distances and the exact final low mesh.
repair_path: Repair local cage, topology, UV, naming, or bake settings; rebake only from the recorded source and rerun target inspection.

failure_library.symptom: An asset looks individually detailed but breaks family scale, surface language, density, or material response in context.
likely_causes: Variants were judged alone.
Texel density, roughness range, wear scale, color space, or channel packing drifted.
A renderer preview was mistaken for target appearance.
checks: Compare density and material response beside accepted family assets under target lighting and camera distance.
Inspect color-space and channel assignments in the target runtime.
repair_path: Restore family constraints, re-export the target material variant, and obtain visual-direction review.

failure_library.symptom: The asset imports mirrored, rotated, scaled incorrectly, offset from the grid, or unusable for placement and animation attachment.
likely_causes: Unit or handedness conversion was implicit.
Transforms were unapplied or double-converted.
Pivot, origin, hierarchy, socket, or naming rules were not target-bound.
checks: Compare source and target units, axes, handedness, transforms, bounds, origin, pivot, hierarchy, and attachment locators.
Place the asset against a known-scale target fixture.
repair_path: Apply the declared conversion once, restore the required pivot/hierarchy, re-export, and verify against the known-scale fixture.

failure_library.symptom: LOD geometry meets numerical budgets but visibly pops, collapses the silhouette, destroys material boundaries, or changes gameplay readability.
likely_causes: Automatic reduction optimized triangle count without protected features.
Transitions were not judged at representative distance, motion, FOV, or lighting.
checks: Measure each LOD and observe transitions in the target runtime from representative cameras and motion.
Compare silhouette, shading, UV/material continuity, sockets, bounds, and collision implications.
repair_path: Protect critical features or rebuild the LOD, tune transition criteria with the technical owner, and repeat visual review.

failure_library.symptom: Collision is missing, too expensive, blocks intended openings, permits penetration, or produces unstable interaction.
likely_causes: Render geometry was used as collision without evidence.
Concavity, primitive naming, transforms, or interaction needs were misunderstood.
Visual fit was accepted without gameplay testing.
checks: Inspect target-side collision, complexity, bounds, openings, transforms, and declared interaction traces.
Run the exact relevant gameplay or physics fixture with the owning roles.
repair_path: Revise simple collision candidates and hand gameplay/physics acceptance to the appropriate engineer or QA role.

failure_library.symptom: The asset imports with no structural errors, but no representative visual, performance, collision, deformation, gameplay, or rights evidence exists.
likely_causes: Importer success was treated as final acceptance.
Evidence surfaces and decision ownership were collapsed.
checks: Build an evidence matrix across source, structural, visual, runtime, performance, interaction, and provenance surfaces.
Identify each missing owner and test context.
repair_path: Narrow the claim to clean import, keep game readiness blocked, and issue the required handoffs.

failure_library.symptom: A reference, texture, scan, kit, generator output, trademark, or likeness contributes to the asset but its allowed use or attribution is unknown.
likely_causes: Source collection outran provenance capture.
Transformation or generation was mistaken for clearance.
checks: Trace every non-original input and derivative relationship.
Retrieve captured terms, author/provider identity, consent, attribution, and intended distribution.
repair_path: Block release use, preserve the evidence, request IP review, and replace the source when clearance cannot be established.

professional_tests.fixture: Create a bounded hard-surface prop from an accepted brief and budget, then reopen, export, validate, import, inspect, and package the exact candidate.
expected_observations: Source, geometry, UV, bake, material, LOD/collision, export, import, visual, measurement, and provenance evidence remain linked and separately labeled.
The specialist records target-context gaps instead of converting clean import into game-ready acceptance.
professional_tests.pass_condition: The exact candidate survives the declared round trip within scoped budgets, visible defects are repaired or recorded, and all adjacent acceptance claims remain correctly handed off.

professional_tests.fixture: Produce a small modular asset family with snap dimensions, shared material logic, variants, LODs, and representative in-context placement.
expected_observations: Scale, pivots, snap, density, material response, silhouette language, names, and source relationships are consistent and measured.
World-layout and art-direction decisions are requested rather than silently invented.
professional_tests.pass_condition: The family works as a traceable system in the declared target context without the specialist absorbing world or direction authority.

professional_tests.fixture: A seeded source/export pair exhibits shading seams caused by triangulation, normals, tangents, or bake mismatch.
expected_observations: The specialist localizes the mismatch using source and target evidence.
Repair preserves editable source and reruns the affected bake, export, and import checks.
professional_tests.pass_condition: The seeded defect is reproduced and repaired or honestly blocked without hiding it through lighting, camera, or material changes.

professional_tests.fixture: An auto-generated LOD passes the triangle target but destroys a critical silhouette and produces visible transition popping.
expected_observations: The numerical pass and visual failure are recorded separately.
The specialist protects critical features, retunes the candidate, and requests technical/art review where required.
professional_tests.pass_condition: The body rejects budget-only success and preserves the unresolved target-context decision until evidence supports it.

professional_tests.fixture: A detailed reference image is provided without target engine, platform, use distance, budgets, material model, collision, LOD, or rights information.
expected_observations: The specialist may create only an explicitly provisional blockout if authorized.
It lists blockers and handoffs instead of fabricating production targets or clearance.
professional_tests.pass_condition: Expensive or irreversible production stops at the correct boundary and the missing contract is returned clearly.

professional_tests.fixture: A GLB passes structural validation and imports cleanly but displays wrong material response, lacks collision evidence, and contains an unknown-license texture.
expected_observations: Structural pass, visual failure, collision NOT_TESTED, and rights BLOCKED remain distinct.
The specialist routes material/runtime diagnosis and rights review to the correct owners.
professional_tests.pass_condition: The candidate is not called game-ready and no missing evidence is polished away.

promotion_requirements: New asset-class capability has source/provenance, explicit ownership, representative success and seeded-failure fixtures, and a rollback or repair route.
New engine, renderer, exporter, format, compression mode, generator, or DCC support is version-bound and tested through the exact target pipeline.
Visual observation and runtime evidence accompany structural validation where the claim depends on appearance or behavior.
Cross-intelligence and adjacent-profession tests distinguish professional machinery from model familiarity and preserve authority boundaries.
